args.command:
PORT=3456 node src/server.mjs &
sleep 1
# Add two books
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "add1: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" -d "title=Dune&author=Frank Herbert&notes=Reading slowly" http://localhost:3456/books
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "add2: %{http_code}\n" -d "title=Piranesi&author=Susanna Clarke" http://localhost:3456/books
# Home page shows both under currently reading
curl -s http://localhost:3456/ | grep -E "Currently reading|Finished|Dune|Piranesi" | head -6
# Get first book's id and view its page (the shareable link)
ID=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('data/books.json'))[0].id)")
echo "--- book page /book/$ID ---"
curl -s http://localhost:3456/book/$ID | grep -E "<h1>|author|notes|Currently reading"
# Mark it finished
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "finish: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" -X POST http://localhost:3456/book/$ID/finish
curl -s http://localhost:3456/book/$ID | grep -E "Finished"
# Edit notes
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "notes: %{http_code}\n" -d "notes=Loved the ending" http://localhost:3456/book/$ID/notes
curl -s http://localhost:3456/book/$ID | grep "Loved"
# Unknown book -> 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "unknown: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3456/book/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
# XSS check: title with script tag is escaped
curl -s -o /dev/null -d "title=<script>alert(1)</script>&author=x" http://localhost:3456/books
curl -s http://localhost:3456/ | grep -c "<script>alert" || echo "escaped OK"
cat data/books.json | head -12

args.content:
# Book tracker

A small, dependency-free app for tracking the books you're reading.

## Run it

```sh
npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:3000 (set `PORT` to use a different port).

## What it does

- The home page lists what you're **currently reading** and what you've **finished**.
- Add a book (title, author, optional notes) from the form on the home page.
- Mark a book as finished from the list or from its own page.
- Click a book to see its title, author, and your notes — and edit the notes there.
- Every book has a stable URL (`/book/<id>`) you can send to someone.

## Storage

No database and no accounts. Books are saved to `data/books.json`, so they
survive a restart. Delete that file to start over.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

events.content:
The book tracker is built and verified working. Run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

I kept it dependency-free: a plain Node HTTP server (`src/server.mjs`) that renders server-side HTML, with all persistence in `src/store.mjs`, which reads and writes `data/books.json`. No database, no accounts, no build step.

What you get:

- **Home page** shows two lists — Currently reading and Finished — plus the add-a-book form (title, author, optional notes).
- **Mark as finished** via a button next to each book in the list, or on the book's own page.
- **Book page** at `/book/<id>` shows the title, author, and your notes, with a textarea to edit the notes. The id is a stable UUID, so that URL is the shareable link.
- **Persistence**: every change is written straight to `data/books.json` (pretty-printed, so it's easy to hand-edit). I verified by adding a book, killing the server, restarting it, and confirming the book was still listed.

I also exercised the whole flow with curl — adding, finishing, editing notes, a 404 for unknown ids — and confirmed user input is HTML-escaped, so a title like `<script>...` renders as text rather than executing. There are six vitest tests for the store (`npm test`), all passing, including one that reopens the JSON file with a fresh store instance to simulate a restart. `data/` is gitignored since it's your personal content.

One small addition beyond the letter of the request: notes are editable on the book page, since notes naturally accumulate while you're reading rather than only at add time. Easy to strip out if you don't want it.
